sentence: A 25-year-old patient comes to the Nutrition Consultation to monitor her nutritional status; seven months earlier she had been diagnosed with Ulcerative Colitis (UC), and during that period she had received treatment with corticosteroids: methylprednisolone 1.5 mg/kg/24 h IV for two months of admission and 30 mg/24 h of oral prednisone in a descending pattern during the remaining five months.

She reported arthralgia in both knees, and her examination showed pain with posterior rotation in both femoral heads, more evident in the right hip, which also had limited internal rotation; The left knee had reduced flexion movement, and when gait was examined, claudication was observed towards the right side.
In the analyzes carried out, no markers of autoimmunity were detected, and plasma concentrations of calcium, phosphorus and vitamin D were within the normal range.
Bone densitometry (BMD) showed osteoporosis in the lumbar spine (T score - 3.1) and osteopenia in the femoral neck (T score - 1.5).

Simple radiographs showed data suggestive of grade II NA in both femoral heads, more evident on the right side; In the knees, an osteochondral lesion was observed in the internal femoral condyle of the left knee with irregularities on its articular surface.
Magnetic resonance imaging confirmed necrosis lesions in both femoral heads and in both knees, both on the tibial and femoral sides.
In the next MRI, performed just 3 months later, signs of sinking in the right hip were already evident.
The patient was treated with alendronate and calcium and vitamin D supplements due to her osteoporosis, corticosteroids were suspended and weight off the affected joints was advised.
